items.title: Jim Robinson Interview, 1961-06-15
items.q: George played all different man with Kid Punch. Last time he left and he played with Kid Punch.

ctx.x: So he played around here, wasn't he? This is home, yeah, sure. He played too.

Who did George play with? Who did George play with? Who did George? Foster. Who George? George played all different man with Kid Punch. Last time he left and he played with Kid Punch. Yeah, with Punch. George left and he went to New York, not New York, Chicago. That's why he made them records with Lewis, you know what I mean? The Kid Oren and Hot Fire. George Foster. He be jeezing all that thing, you know what I mean? He made all that stuff, you know what I mean? Muscat Rambles. George and all that recording.
Did you play with a brass band in different range? No. Did you ever play with any brass bands here in the city?

items.title: Jim Robinson Interview, 1961-07-13
items.q: Me and Joy, and, and, and, uh, George, and, uh, George Foster, and, uh, Zulie Sing on drum

ctx.x: Yeah. With Lee. Yeah. I worked with Lee. But three years ago, in New York. We played all at the, Town Club. Me and Joy Lewis. With Lee, with Lee, yeah. Mm-hmm. Lee came from Chicago, and, but I saw it in New York. Me and Joy played with him. Me and Joy played with him. Me and Joy, and, and, and, uh, George, and, uh, George Foster, and, uh, Zulie Sing on drum,…
That was only two or three years ago?

items.title: Percy Humphrey Band: Percy Humphrey, Jim Robinson, Ernest Roubleau, Josiah Frazier Interview, 1972-02-29
items.q: Now where the kicks come out, like I had them laughing by the Pop Foster.

ctx.x: So far as the rock and roll. I keep instrument to play rock and roll in case if somebody jumped me up. I keep that kind of instrument to play rock and roll. But see like this, this ain't no rock and roll instrument.

You see, let me tell them this too. You see they speak about saying music is a universal language. My first time going overseas in 1966. We had a place they called Copenhagen, Munich, Germany. Because it was working out of Frankfurt, Germany. The first night we played, the first number you played, everybody sounds looking at you in Germany. You think they're not. They're taking that music. They couldn't understand our language. And I'm from the south down here. My way of speaking, where the kicks will come out…
Especially the Dixieland jazz. It reaches so many, many people. What about keeping time? Did y'all keep good time there? Did people dance to the bands?
